root_topic: A Journey through States of Water

branches.theme: 8.1 Three Physical States and Phase Transitions

details: Water exists as Solid (Ice), Liquid (Water), and Gas (Water Vapor).
Melting: Solid ice turns into liquid water upon heating.
Freezing: Liquid water turns into solid ice upon cooling.
Evaporation: Liquid water transforms into water vapor upon heating.
Condensation: Water vapor cools down and turns into liquid water droplets.
experiments_or_examples: Observing ice melting in a beaker, steam condensing on a plate, and water freezing in a tray

details: Evaporation occurs continuously at all temperatures from exposed water surfaces.
Evaporation rate increases with: (1) Higher temperature/sunlight, (2) Larger exposed surface area, (3) Increased wind speed, (4) Lower humidity.
experiments_or_examples: Bottle Cap vs Wide Plate Experiment: Equal water volumes evaporate much faster in a wide plate due to larger surface area

branches.theme: 8.3 The Natural Water Cycle and Cloud Formation

details: Solar radiation heat evaporates water from oceans, rivers, and soil, plus plant transpiration.
Rising warm vapor cools at high altitudes and condenses into microscopic floating water droplets around dust particles, forming clouds.
Droplets combine; when heavy, precipitation falls as rain or snow, returning water to Earth.
experiments_or_examples: Simulating cloud formation inside a glass jar with ice lid and warm water

details: Bawadis (Stepwells): Traditional Indian architecture (e.g., Toorji ka Jhalra in Jodhpur) designed to collect rainwater, shade water from evaporation, and recharge aquifers.
Atmospheric Water Generators (AWGs): Modern technology condensing drinking water directly from ambient atmospheric air humidity.
experiments_or_examples: Rainwater harvesting models and AWG installations
